chunks: Bashīr al-Nabbāl asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about fasting on the Day of Doubt, so he said:
"Fast it. If it is from Shaʿbān, it is voluntary; and if it is from the month of Ramaḍān, then it is a day you were granted success to fast."

key_terms.يَوْمِ الشَّكِّ: the day of uncertainty about whether Ramaḍān has begun

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting the Day of Doubt before Ramadan in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning fasting on Yawm al-Shakk, the day when it is uncertain whether the month has shifted from Shaʿbān to Ramaḍān. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that one may fast it, and the fast is counted as voluntary if it is still Shaʿbān, while if it is in fact Ramaḍān, then one has been divinely enabled to fast a day of Ramaḍān.
